subject: [PATCH v8 00/14] mm: thp: always enable mTHP support

reviews.author: Luiz Capitulino
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch's assumption about PMD page support is incorrect, as some architectures like x86 have conditional support and may lack PSE bit presence even on 64-bit systems; he also pointed out that has_transparent_hugepage() has different semantics on certain architectures and should not be used to gate all THP support.
sentiment_signals: pointed out semantic differences in has_transparent_hugepage()
reviews.raw_body:
No :)

The architectures that have conditional PMD page support (ie. discovered
at run-time via has_transparent_hugepage()) are x86, s390, powerpc and
mips.

For x86 for example, even on 64-bit there are cases where the PSE bit
may not be present (eg. some errata and by hypervisor CPUID masking).

That being said, the main goal of the series is that
has_transparent_hugepage() is overloaded: it has different semantics on
those architectures and is used to gate all THP support (which is not
the right thing to do for mTHP).

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) requested follow-up work on PUD support cleanup, specifically reworking the CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE_PUD magic.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, and I hope that we can then follow-up with similar PUD support cleanup to
rework some of that CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE_PUD magic.

-- 
Cheers,

David

2026-09-18.patch_summary: This patch enables support for mTHP (machine-specific THP) on all CPUs, addressing a limitation in the previous series where some CPUs lacked PMD-sized page support.
